prize_parts.citation: For chemically induced targeted protein degradation: the design of bifunctional molecules that direct a chosen protein to an E3 ubiquitin ligase, and the discovery that thalidomide-type drugs act by reprogramming cereblon

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: one part, B012, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. After round 1 I can state the unifying achievement in one sentence: a small molecule can be made to bring a protein of the chemist's choice to an E3 ligase, either by design (PROTACs) or by reshaping the ligase surface (thalidomide-type glues acting through cereblon), so that the cell destroys the protein. That is event-driven pharmacology built on molecular recognition, ternary-complex cooperativity and kinetics, and it is reproduced across many laboratories and E3 ligases. It is also the one shortlisted candidate that eight of eight members ranked, with four in the top three, so the disagreement is about names and timing and not about whether the science is real. Cereblon sits under the glue branch and under most clinical PROTACs, so Handa's identification of the target links the two lineages into a single mechanistic story. Crews and Deshaies supply the concept and its first demonstrations.
statement.case_against: The chair's question about one citation versus two is the weak point. If the committee reads the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism as separate discoveries, my wording joins things that some members would keep apart, and Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures remain unrecognised. No degrader is approved, so the therapeutic payoff is not yet shown. A reasonable member can conclude the field should wait a year or more rather than force an eight-name field into three seats. I have no verified information on late-stage trial outcomes, so I do not rest the case on them.

responses.point: Linke asked me to say how one citation can cover both the PROTAC design and the cereblon work of Handa, and disagreed with my first-round view that Liu alone would be enough for base editing.
responses.response: My answer on the citation is that the shared object is the E3 ligase as a programmable recruiter. A PROTAC works by bringing a chosen target to a ligase through a designed bifunctional molecule, and a glue works by reshaping the ligase surface so that new substrates are recruited. Cereblon is the ligase on which both converge, so the citation names induced degradation by small molecules and then the two routes in a subordinate clause. I accept that this is a judgement and not a proof of a single lineage. On base editing you have moved me. The adenine editor needed an enzyme evolved to act on DNA, and that is a real scientific step, so if the committee goes to B060 I would credit Liu, Komor and Gaudelli and not Liu alone. I still hold B060 as my second choice because of its proximity to the 2020 prize and the unresolved Target-AID attribution.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B012 second but argues that the PROTAC lineage (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) and the cereblon lineage (Handa, Ito) are different discoveries, that three seats cannot cover them fairly, and that the committee should hold the field for a later year.
responses.response: The lineages did arise separately, and I do not dispute that. I disagree that this argues for waiting. A prize for the field will always leave out real contributors, as the three-name rule does for B060 as well, where Kondo and Nishida are omitted in your own configuration. The case for acting now is that the mechanism is already reproduced independently and the induced-proximity principle is established. Deferral does not make the attribution cleaner, because Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito remain in the field next year. The convergence on cereblon is what lets me defend two strands under one citation, and it is why I chose Handa and not Ciulli for the third seat. I do give weight to your point about arbitrariness, and it is the main reason I keep B060 as a serious alternative if the committee finds B012's names indefensible.

responses.point: Zou weighs Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures most, sees Handa's cereblon discovery as a separate strand, and would rank B012 higher only if the PROTAC versus molecular-glue split is settled.
responses.response: I agree that Ciulli's structures show how induced proximity works at atomic detail, and that is the part of the field I find most chemically satisfying. The reason I still put Handa in the third seat is that the structural work shows how proximity works for ligases that were already usable, while identifying cereblon as the thalidomide target is what explained a drug in clinical use and opened the glue branch. Both are real, and the choice between them is a weighing of target identification against structural design, not a question of who is more rigorous. If the committee prefers the structural framing, a Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli configuration with a PROTAC-only citation would also be defensible to me. I would not go further than that and treat the split as settled, because I do not think the evidence in the files can settle it.

responses.point: Brzezinski supports Crews, Deshaies and Handa, agrees that Handa lifts the prize from a drug-design strategy to a mechanism, and asks that the case rest on the concept and confirmed mechanism and not on unconfirmed clinical readouts.
responses.response: I accept the correction. My first-round maturity argument leaned on the size of the clinical pipeline, and I cannot confirm late-stage outcomes from the material I have. The case I make now rests on independent reproduction of the mechanism, structural definition of the ternary complex and the breadth of E3 ligases used, with the clinic as supporting but not decisive evidence. That makes B012 a prize for a mechanistic principle that is already secure, and it keeps the lack of an approved drug as a timing risk I name openly and not as part of the argument.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats PROTAC design and cereblon-dependent glue mechanism as one achievement or two, and whether a single citation of the kind I propose is accepted as honest.
Whether Handa or Ciulli should hold the third seat. I would accept either, but I cannot show from the record that one claim is stronger.
How much the absence of an approved degrader should count. I cannot confirm any late-stage trial result and do not rely on one.
Whether B060, with a clearer single principle but proximity to the 2020 prize and the Target-AID attribution, is the better-defined choice for a majority.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on B012, B060 or the other shortlisted entries. Scientific proximity only: my research overlaps with Emma Sparr in peptide and lipid self-assembly and I work on nanoparticle and peptide biosensing, which relates to B019 and B061 but is not the same work. My postdoc mentors Molly Stevens and Freddy Boey are not credited on any shortlisted entry. I flag the overlap for the committee to judge and have no change from round 1.
